rationale: CR-001 is resolved. The fix-up pins the default-value test to the repo's shipped customer-config.yaml via a module-level SHIPPED_CUSTOMER_CONFIG derived from the test file's own location (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]), so it no longer depends on the env-overridable CUSTOMER_CONFIG_DIR BaseSettings field, and it now asserts through get_enabled_components() — the list GET /v1/config actually serves — instead of the raw .components parse result. The assertion was mutation-checked rather than assumed: loading a copy of the shipped YAML with the allowedImageDomains entry stripped makes the lookup return None, so assertIsNotNone fails, confirming the test would catch a regression that drops the item from the served list. 35 tests pass across both config test files and ruff format/check are clean on the changed file. The fix-up diff touches one test file only (+8/-3, no production code), introducing no new security, public-API, data-loss or runtime-correctness surface, so no confirmation pass was dispatched. business_review and standards_review are carried forward unchanged from the final round.

business_review.item: AC1 — GET /v1/config includes an item with id allowedImageDomains whose settings.value is the configured comma-separated domain string
business_review.notes: config/customer/customer-config.yaml adds `- id: "allowedImageDomains"`; the id is absent from CONFIG_IDS (customer_config.py:24-30) so get_enabled_components() (customer_config.py:188-197) passes it through the YAML branch unfiltered, and `value` survives because ComponentSetting sets extra="allow" (customer_config.py:41). Router test asserts the configured string is echoed verbatim through the HTTP layer

business_review.item: AC2 — Value configurable per deployment through the same mechanism other customer config values use
business_review.notes: No per-item Helm value or env var exists for any config item. deploy-templates/values.yaml:513-529 mounts the externally managed ConfigMap codemie-customer-config over /app/config/customer, and config.py:112 points CUSTOMER_CONFIG_DIR there. Configured exactly like bannerMessage/mcpAuthTimeoutSeconds; no chart template renders customer-config.yaml, so no values.yaml change is appropriate

business_review.item: AC3 — Unconfigured: omitted or empty value; never fails, never a default domain list
business_review.notes: Shipped default is value: "" — no invented domains. A missing/null value would be dropped entirely by response_model_exclude_none=True (routers/customer_config.py:28), which the UI's `?? ''` handles. Both branches tested (test_allowed_image_domains_default_is_empty, test_get_config_with_unset_allowed_image_domains)

business_review.item: AC4 — Every user who can open a chat receives the item, external users included
business_review.notes: GET /v1/config carries no auth dependency (router declared dependencies=[], routers/customer_config.py:21-30) and availableForExternal is only a model field (customer_config.py:35, default True) — grep confirms no server-side filtering exists anywhere in src/. The YAML entry omits the field so it defaults to True; confirmed True in a live dump

business_review.item: AC5 — Existing config items unchanged; no breaking change to the response shape
business_review.notes: Diff is additive only: one YAML list entry plus tests. No change to Component/ComponentSetting or the router. No other test in tests/ loads the real customer-config.yaml or asserts a component count that an addition could break

business_review.item: AC6 — Tests follow the repo's existing config-endpoint test pattern (set / unset branches)
business_review.notes: Set/unset pairs at both layers; router tests mirror the mock_customer_config fixture style of test_get_config_with_mcp_auth_origin. Partially undercut by CR-001 at the config layer, where the unset test deviated from the class's patching pattern — resolved in the fix-up
Literal id: "allowedImageDomains" in the YAML; same casing asserted in both test files and confirmed in the live component dump

business_review.item: Backend stores/returns the raw comma-separated string; implements no hostname matching
business_review.notes: No matching, splitting, normalization or validation code anywhere in the diff — the value is a plain extra field returned verbatim via jsonable_encoder. Router test asserts a byte-identical round-trip of "raw.githubusercontent.com,.example.com,cdn.customer.io"

business_review.item: Item appears in the same ConfigItem[] array with the list in settings.value, readable exactly like bannerMessage
business_review.notes: Same array from the same handler, same {id, settings:{enabled, value, availableForExternal}} shape as bannerMessage/mcpAuthOrigin

business_review.item: Mirror the existing string-config pattern; no new endpoint, config mechanism or storage location
business_review.notes: The only production change is one entry in the existing components list. No new router, no CONFIG_IDS entry (correct — the value is customer YAML, not runtime-derived like idpProvider/mcpAuthOrigin), no new env var, no new Helm plumbing

business_review.item: Verify whether /v1/config filters by availableForExternal or auth/tenant scope before relying on visibility
business_review.notes: Verified rather than assumed: no filter exists. get_enabled_components() filters only on settings.enabled and runtime-id exclusion; the endpoint is unauthenticated

business_review.item: Out of scope respected — no hostname matching/validation, no change to image fetching/proxying
business_review.notes: Diff touches only customer-config.yaml and two test files (3 files, +90/-0). No image fetch/proxy code touched
Conforms to configuration-patterns.md (use the existing YAML config tree for runtime settings, no direct env reads) and testing-patterns.md (tests mirror src/ under the nearest existing test dirs)

standards_review.notes: The single commit in origin/main..HEAD, "EPMCDME-12950: Expose image allow-list via customer config", matches the EPMCDME-####: Description form required by .ai-run/guides/standards/git-workflow.md; no conventional-commit prefix
poetry run ruff format + ruff check clean on both changed test files, per .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md

Checked against .ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md. No secret is added or logged; the value is an operator-chosen hostname list, not a credential. Broad visibility on an unauthenticated endpoint is required by AC4 and is the pre-existing posture of /v1/config, not introduced here. The backend deliberately performs no matching, so no security decision is taken server-side — the enforcement boundary stays in the UI where the ticket places it

finding_status.notes: tests/codemie/configs/test_customer_config.py now defines SHIPPED_CUSTOMER_CONFIG = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "config/customer/customer-config.yaml" and passes it as config_path, removing the dependency on the env-overridable CUSTOMER_CONFIG_DIR BaseSettings field and on the installed-package layout; the lookup moved from config.components to config.get_enabled_components(), so the test now covers the list the endpoint serves. A comment records why the path is pinned. Verified by mutation rather than assertion alone: with the allowedImageDomains entry stripped from a copy of the shipped YAML, get_enabled_components() returns no such component (lookup -> None), so assertIsNotNone fails — the test does catch the regression it is meant to catch. 35 tests pass; ruff format/check clean.
